newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks dive again, Nikkei ends down 2.57%.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks dive again, Nikkei ends down 2.57%.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's rally over the past two days fizzled on Thursday, as the key market index lost close to 500 points, hurt by lingering worries about the banking sector, brokers said.
The market's benchmark index, Nikkei 225 average, dropped by 471.26 points, or 2.57 percent, to end at 17,864.04. It fell as low as 17,781.89 at one point.
"There were no investors to aggressively buy cash stocks," said a fund manager at a foreign trust bank.
The dollar's retreat on Thursday halted purchases of export-oriented blue chips, which led the rally over the past few days.

Comments by an influential finance ministry official on Thursday helped to stem the rise of the dollar. Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying that Japan would intervene in the foreign exchange markets when the timing is effective.
